overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Dreyfus's critique of symbolic AI. You'll be asked about the four assumptions of symbolic AI, the relevance problem, the five-stage model of skill acquisition, and the phenomenological sources of the critique.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Which of Dreyfus's assumptions holds that the world consists of independent facts, each representable by a symbol?

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Dreyfus treated it as the deepest of the four, since the others depend on it.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The epistemological assumption concerns whether all knowledge can be formalized.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The psychological assumption concerns whether the mind follows formal rules.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The biological assumption concerns whether the brain works like a digital computer.

forms.stemHtml: Why doesn't adding rules for relevance solve the relevance problem, on Dreyfus's argument?

options.html: Computers can't store enough rules to cover every case
options.text: Computers can't store enough rules to cover every case
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The problem isn't storage. Each rule must be applied, which raises the problem again.

options.html: Applying each rule requires finding what's relevant again
options.text: Applying each rule requires finding what's relevant again
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Recognizing when a rule applies is the same problem, so adding rules starts a regress.

options.html: Relevance rules would contradict the rules they govern
options.text: Relevance rules would contradict the rules they govern
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The problem is a regress, not a contradiction.

options.html: Relevance can't be expressed in any symbolic language
options.text: Relevance can't be expressed in any symbolic language
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Relevance rules can be written. The trouble is that applying them raises the problem again.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately describe the Dreyfus five-stage model of skill acquisition? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Novices apply rules to context-free features
options.text: Novices apply rules to context-free features
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Context-free features can be recognized without experience.

options.html: Competent performers choose a plan and feel responsible for the outcome
options.text: Competent performers choose a plan and feel responsible for the outcome

options.html: Experts usually see what to do without deliberating
options.text: Experts usually see what to do without deliberating
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In normal cases, experts respond intuitively.

options.html: Experts apply the novice's rules faster and more reliably
options.text: Experts apply the novice's rules faster and more reliably
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. On the model, experts no longer need the rules. The change is one of kind.

options.html: Proficient performers decide intuitively but perceive by rules
options.text: Proficient performers decide intuitively but perceive by rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's the reverse: they see intuitively what's going on, but decide deliberately.

forms.stemHtml: What is Dreyfus's name for the problem of how a system determines which of the facts it could represent matter in a given situation? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Rules for relevance only restate it.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The answer is "relevance problem."

forms.stemHtml: Which claim did Dreyfus take from Heidegger in his critique of symbolic AI?

options.html: The brain processes information as a digital computer does
options.text: The brain processes information as a digital computer does
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the biological assumption, which Dreyfus rejected.

options.html: Skill is stored in the body as a set of explicit rules
options.text: Skill is stored in the body as a set of explicit rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. For Dreyfus, skill isn't a matter of explicit rules.

options.html: A world of significance isn't a set of independent facts
options.text: A world of significance isn't a set of independent facts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Facts show up as relevant only within a context of purposes that's already in place.

options.html: Thinking is the manipulation of symbols by formal rules
options.text: Thinking is the manipulation of symbols by formal rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the psychological assumption, which Dreyfus rejected.

title: Dreyfus and the Critique of AI
